$comment: Codelist governance registry — the machine-readable form of docs/codelist-governance.md. Hand-authored (the four axes are GOVERNANCE/implementation decisions, not derivable). One entry per codelist, keyed by the canonical codelist NAME used in our profiles and sidecar `codelist` values. Read by the instance-schema generator (inlineEnum) and the codelist/UI service (useForUI, externalSource). A consistency test (governance.test.mjs) cross-checks `shipped` against the .gc directory and `schematronValidated` against the CVA, so this file cannot silently drift from the repo.

$axes.shipped: A .gc exists under ESPD-EDM/codelists/. (Property of ESPD-EDM.)
$axes.schematronValidated: The CVA/Schematron enforces the value set at the XML interchange layer. (Property of the STANDARD — set by ESPD governance; we only read it.)
$axes.useForUI: The service should offer these codes as the pick list. (UI/UX decision.)
$axes.inlineEnum: Our JSON Schema carries the values as an enum, vs referencing the list by name. (OUR implementation decision, driven mainly by size/stability — small, stable lists are convenient to inline; large lists are referenced by name.)

$axesAreIndependent: The four axes are INDEPENDENT; do not infer one from another. In particular `inlineEnum` and `schematronValidated` do NOT correlate — all four combinations are legitimate: a small closed list can be BOTH validated AND inlined (docrefcontent-type, eoid-type); a large validated list is referenced by name (country, occupation); a small unvalidated list is inlined as a suggestion (financial-ratio-type, boolean-gui-control-type). The only derived property is the marker below.
$codelistEnumIsImplementerChoice: A SEPARATE, derived marker on an inlined enum, true iff (inlineEnum && !schematronValidated): the inlined values are our SUGGESTED set rather than an enforced one. When a list is both validated and inlined, the enum is inlined for authoring convenience but the values are the standard's enforced set, so the marker is false.

country.$note: 341 codes; validated/closed; too large to inline usefully -> reference by name; UI picker from the service. Team table.

occupation.$note: 4046 ESCO codes; validated/closed; hierarchical; too large to inline -> reference by name. Team table.

financial-ratio-type.$note: 40 codes; shipped but NOT Schematron-validated => inlined enum is a SUGGESTED set (implementer choice). Team table.

boolean-gui-control-type.$note: 6 codes; shipped but NOT validated => suggested, inlined (implementer choice). See docs M1: whether a GUI-control code belongs in the data model at all is a separate concern. Team table.

procurement-procedure-type.$note: NOT shipped (ESPD-EDM issue #308). Needed for UI + inlined as a suggested set. Until the .gc ships, the enum is hand-maintained from the OP dataset. Team table; see improvement-ideas.md X1.

docrefcontent-type.$note: 10 codes; validated (cac:AdditionalDocumentReference/cbc:DocumentTypeCode) AND inlined (Part I Section A). The valid 'validated + inlined' case: small enough to inline for authoring-time feedback, while the XML layer enforces the same set. Enum is NOT implementer-choice (values are the enforced set).

eoid-type.$note: 5 codes; validated (cac:PartyIdentification/cbc:ID/@schemeID) AND inlined (Part I Section B). Same 'validated + inlined' case as docrefcontent-type. Enum is NOT implementer-choice.

access-right.$note: Validated (cbc:ConfidentialityLevelCode). Not in the team's five; axes recorded from repo ground truth. REVIEW: inlineEnum is a size/stability call we have not yet needed to make (no modelled field uses it).

currency.$note: ~290 codes; validated (cbc:ValueCurrencyCode, @currencyID); too large to inline -> reference by name. Repo ground truth. REVIEW.

eo-role-type.$note: 5 codes; validated (RoleCode). Small enough that we COULD inline it (like eoid-type) when the Part V OT criterion / EO role is modelled — revisit then. Currently reference by name. Repo ground truth. REVIEW.

economic-operator-size.$note: Validated (IndustryClassificationCode). Not yet used by a modelled field. Repo ground truth. REVIEW.

criterion-element-type.$note: Internal EDM structural code (cbc:TypeCode = REQUIREMENT/QUESTION/...), not a user-facing value. Validated; not a UI picker. Repo ground truth. REVIEW.

property-group-type.$note: Internal structural code (ON*/ONTRUE/ONFALSE on PropertyGroupTypeCode). Not user-facing. Repo ground truth. REVIEW.

response-data-type.$note: Internal value-type code (cbc:ValueDataTypeCode); authoritative for our value-type registry's keys. Not a user picker. Repo ground truth. REVIEW.

profile-execution-id.$note: Document-envelope profile id. Fixed per document, not a user picker. Repo ground truth. REVIEW.

selection-criterion.$note: Criterion-id authority (cbc:CriterionTypeCode for selection criteria). Structural, not a free user picker. Repo ground truth. REVIEW.

exclusion-ground.$note: Criterion-id authority (cbc:CriterionTypeCode for exclusion grounds). Structural. Repo ground truth. REVIEW.

criterion.$note: ⚠ DISCREPANCY surfaced by the consistency test. Our codelist-attribute profile names a 'criterion' list (listID .../authority/criterion, v20240612-0) for cbc:CriterionTypeCode, but NO Criterion.gc is shipped and the CVA validates CriterionTypeCode via the SPLIT lists selection-criterion + exclusion-ground instead. So 'criterion' is an older/umbrella reference that no shipped .gc backs and the CVA does not use. REVIEW: either repoint the attribute profile to selection-criterion/exclusion-ground, or confirm 'criterion' is the intended umbrella listID. Not Schematron-validated as 'criterion' (the split lists are).
